# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and widely supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git, MPI, certificates, and required runtime libraries
# - build-essential: Provides compilers (gcc, g++) and make
# - gfortran: Fortran compiler, often needed for HPC codes
# - git: To clone the source code repository
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development headers
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone)
# - libgomp1: GNU OpenMP library, a specific requirement
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image slim and clean up apt cache
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# This forces communication over the TCP network interface (eth0) and
# disables shared-memory (sm) transport across different pods, preventing errors.
RUN echo "btl = tcp,self" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Clone the latest branch of the AMG (amg2023) source code into /opt
WORKDIR /opt
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git

# Set the working directory to the root of the cloned repository
WORKDIR /opt/AMG

# FIX: Build all required libraries first, then the final executable.
# The makefiles in each subdirectory build a required static library.
# The makefile in 'test' links them all together, which caused the previous linker error.
RUN make -C utilities && \
    make -C krylov && \
    make -C IJ_mv && \
    make -C seq_mv && \
    make -C parcsr_mv && \
    make -C parcsr_ls && \
    make -C test

# Copy the compiled 'amg' binary from its build location to a system-wide PATH.
RUN cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg

# Clean up the source code to reduce the final image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/AMG

# Set a default working directory for when the container starts
WORKDIR /root

# The image is now built with the 'amg' executable on the PATH.
# The container can be run with a command such as:
# mpirun -np <number_of_procs> amg [amg_options]

Hello! As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the provided code and error logs. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the failure is a missing shared library at runtime. The key error message from the logs is:

```
amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This error, combined with the exit code `127`, indicates that when the `amg` executable was launched, the dynamic linker could not find the required OpenMP library (`libgomp.so.1`).

Although the application container's Dockerfile correctly installs the `libgomp1` package, the environment set up by the Flux framework's launcher container does not correctly point to the library's location.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we must explicitly tell the application where to find its required libraries by setting the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable. The standard location for this library in an Ubuntu 22.04-based container is `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`.

I will add this environment variable to your application container definition within the MiniCluster manifest.

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
    environment:
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:tag-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 4
```

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the AMG2023 benchmark on a single AWS CPU node.
# It is configured for a small test problem size as per the requirements.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg-test-aws
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for a single-node execution.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) to run.
  tasks: 4
  # Keep pods and logs after the job finishes for debugging purposes.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux Operator logging settings.
  logging:
    # Fail on any non-zero exit code.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute the AMG benchmark.
      # '-problem 2' is specified as required.
      # '-n 4 4 4' sets a small problem size for testing (not exceeding 4 in any dimension).
      command: "amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4"
      # This container is a worker, not a launcher pod. The Flux Operator
      # will add a launcher pod to submit the job to the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

Hello! As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the provided code and error logs. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the failure is a missing shared library at runtime. The key error message from the logs is:

```
amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This error, combined with the exit code `127`, indicates that when the `amg` executable was launched, the dynamic linker could not find the required OpenMP library (`libgomp.so.1`).

Although the application container's Dockerfile correctly installs the `libgomp1` package, the environment set up by the Flux framework's launcher container does not correctly point to the library's location.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we must explicitly tell the application where to find its required libraries by setting the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable. The standard location for this library in an Ubuntu 22.04-based container is `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`.

I will add this environment variable to your application container definition within the MiniCluster manifest.

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
    environment:
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:tag-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 4
```

The key error message from the logs is:
`amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`

This, combined with the container's exit code of `127`, points to a missing runtime dependency. The `libgomp.so.1` library is essential for running applications compiled with OpenMP support. The `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` currently set in the manifest does not include the directory where this library is located within the container.

### PROPOSED FIX

To resolve this, I will update the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to include `/usr/lib64`, a standard location for such libraries.

Additionally, to align with the optimization and testing goals you provided, I will make the following changes:
1.  **Select an Optimal Instance:** I have chosen the `r6a.12xlarge` instance, which provides the best memory-per-core ratio (16 GiB/core) and a high core count (24), satisfying the optimization goal. A `nodeSelector` will be added to target this instance.

Hello! As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the provided code and error logs. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the failure is a missing shared library at runtime. The key error message from the logs is:

```
amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This error, combined with the exit code `127`, indicates that when the `amg` executable was launched, the dynamic linker could not find the required OpenMP library (`libgomp.so.1`).

Although the application container's Dockerfile correctly installs the `libgomp1` package, the environment set up by the Flux framework's launcher container does not correctly point to the library's location.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we must explicitly tell the application where to find its required libraries by setting the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable. The standard location for this library in an Ubuntu 22.04-based container is `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`.

I will add this environment variable to your application container definition within the MiniCluster manifest.

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
    environment:
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:tag-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 4
```

An analysis of the error log indicates the job failed because the application could not find a required shared library.

### ERROR ANALYSIS

The key error message from the logs is:
`amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`

This, combined with the container's exit code of `127`, points to a missing runtime dependency. The `libgomp.so.1` library is essential for running applications compiled with OpenMP support. The `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` currently set in the manifest does not include the directory where this library is located within the container.

### PROPOSED FIX

To resolve this, I will update the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to include `/usr/lib64`, a standard location for such libraries.

Additionally, to align with the optimization and testing goals you provided, I will make the following changes:
1.  **Select an Optimal Instance:** I have chosen the `r6a.12xlarge` instance, which provides the best memory-per-core ratio (16 GiB/core) and a high core count (24), satisfying the optimization goal. A `nodeSelector` will be added to target this instance.
2.  **Update Tasks and Command:** The number of tasks will be set to 24 to match the vCPU count of the selected instance, preventing oversubscription. The command is updated to a larger problem size as instructed for optimization.
3.  **Add Optimization Environment Variable:** The `OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism` variable will be added as suggested.
4.  **Enable Quiet Logging:** Logging will be set to quiet to reduce noise.

Here is the corrected Job manifest:

```yaml

metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The backoffLimit is set to 1 as requested

  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 128 128 128 -P 4 3 2
    environment:
      # Fix: Added /usr/lib64 to the library path to find libgomp.so.1
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib64

        node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
```

**Analysis of the Error:**

The job failed with an exit code of 127. The logs show the specific reason for this failure:

```
amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This indicates that the `amg` application, which is compiled with OpenMP for threading, cannot find its required OpenMP runtime library (`libgomp.so.1`) in the container's environment. The existing `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` does not include the directory where this library is located.

Additionally, the job manifest is missing a `nodeSelector` to target a specific instance type, which is a requirement for the optimization task.

**Recommended Solution:**

To resolve the library issue, we must update the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable to include the path where system software libraries are stored in this container. Based on the file paths visible in the logs (e.g., `/opt/software/...`), a likely location for these libraries is `/opt/software/lib64`.

To fulfill the optimization requirements, I have also selected an instance type that maximizes the memory per CPU core. The `r6a.12xlarge` instance provides 16 GiB of memory per CPU core (384 GiB / 24 CPU), satisfying the optimization goal. A `nodeSelector` has been added to ensure the job runs on this specific instance type.

Here is the corrected MiniCluster manifest:

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
    environment:
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /opt/software/lib64:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib64
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 4
```

# This MiniCluster manifest incorporates the cumulative debugging feedback.
# The primary fix is to update the LD_LIBRARY_PATH to include /usr/lib64,
# in addition to the standard Ubuntu paths for x86_64 and aarch64.
# This ensures the dynamic linker searches all potential locations for the
# required 'libgomp.so.1' library, resolving the persistent loading error.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg-test-aws
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for a single-node execution.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) to run.
  tasks: 4

  # Keep pods and logs after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Retry the job at most once upon failure.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Pod-specific settings for the MiniCluster.
  pod:
    # Do not restart pods if they fail; let the job controller handle it.
    restartPolicy: Never

  # Flux Operator logging settings.
  logging:
    # Fail on any non-zero exit code.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute the AMG benchmark with the required problem and a small test size.
      command: "amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4"
      # The application container is a worker, not a launcher, per instructions.
      launcher: false
      # Environment variables to fix runtime errors and control threading.
      environment:
        # Constrain OpenMP to a single thread per task to avoid oversubscription.
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        # Set a comprehensive library path to resolve the "libgomp.so.1" loading error.
        LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib64

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the AMG2023 benchmark on a single AWS CPU node.
# It is configured for a small test problem size as per the requirements.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg-test-aws
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for a single-node execution.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) to run.
  tasks: 4
  # Keep pods and logs after the job finishes for debugging purposes.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux Operator logging settings.
  logging:
    # Fail on any non-zero exit code.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute the AMG benchmark.
      # '-problem 2' is specified as required.
      # '-n 4 4 4' sets a small problem size for testing (not exceeding 4 in any dimension).
      command: "amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4"
      # This container is a worker, not a launcher pod. The Flux Operator
      # will add a launcher pod to submit the job to the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

Hello! As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the provided code and error logs. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the failure is a missing shared library at runtime. The key error message from the logs is:

```
amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This error, combined with the exit code `127`, indicates that when the `amg` executable was launched, the dynamic linker could not find the required OpenMP library (`libgomp.so.1`).

Although the application container's Dockerfile correctly installs the `libgomp1` package, the environment set up by the Flux framework's launcher container does not correctly point to the library's location.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we must explicitly tell the application where to find its required libraries by setting the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable. The standard location for this library in an Ubuntu 22.04-based container is `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`.

I will add this environment variable to your application container definition within the MiniCluster manifest.

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
    environment:
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:tag-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 4
```

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest reinstates the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable,
# which has been identified as the correct solution for the persistent
# "libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file" error. This ensures the
# dynamic linker can find the required OpenMP libraries at runtime.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg-test-aws
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for a single-node execution.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) to run.
  tasks: 4

  # Keep pods and logs after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Retry the job at most once upon failure.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Pod-specific settings for the MiniCluster.

result.item:
An analysis of the error log indicates the job failed because the application could not find a required shared library.

### ERROR ANALYSIS

The key error message from the logs is:
`amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`

This, combined with the container's exit code of `127`, points to a missing runtime dependency. The `libgomp.so.1` library is essential for running applications compiled with OpenMP support. The `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` currently set in the manifest does not include the directory where this library is located within the container.

### PROPOSED FIX

To resolve this, I will update the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to include `/usr/lib64`, a standard location for such libraries.

Additionally, to align with the optimization and testing goals you provided, I will make the following changes:
1.  **Select an Optimal Instance:** I have chosen the `r6a.12xlarge` instance, which provides the best memory-per-core ratio (16 GiB/core) and a high core count (24), satisfying the optimization goal. A `nodeSelector` will be added to target this instance.
2.  **Update Tasks and Command:** The number of tasks will be set to 24 to match the vCPU count of the selected instance, preventing oversubscription. The command is updated to a larger problem size as instructed for optimization.
3.  **Add Optimization Environment Variable:** The `OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism` variable will be added as suggested.
4.  **Enable Quiet Logging:** Logging will be set to quiet to reduce noise.

Here is the corrected Job manifest:

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The backoffLimit is set to 1 as requested
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 128 128 128 -P 4 3 2
    environment:
      # Fix: Added /usr/lib64 to the library path to find libgomp.so.1
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib64
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
      # Added suggested optimization variable
      OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  logging:
    # Enabled quiet logging as requested
    quiet: true
  pod:
    restartPolicy: Never
    spec:
      # Added nodeSelector to target the optimal instance
      nodeSelector:
        node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
  # Set size to 1 node as required
  size: 1
  # Increased tasks to match the vCPU count of the selected node
  tasks: 24
```

**Analysis of the Error:**

The job failed with an exit code of 127. The logs show the specific reason for this failure:

```
amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This indicates that the `amg` application, which is compiled with OpenMP for threading, cannot find its required OpenMP runtime library (`libgomp.so.1`) in the container's environment. The existing `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` does not include the directory where this library is located.

Additionally, the job manifest is missing a `nodeSelector` to target a specific instance type, which is a requirement for the optimization task.

**Recommended Solution:**

To resolve the library issue, we must update the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable to include the path where system software libraries are stored in this container. Based on the file paths visible in the logs (e.g., `/opt/software/...`), a likely location for these libraries is `/opt/software/lib64`.

To fulfill the optimization requirements, I have also selected an instance type that maximizes the memory per CPU core. The `r6a.12xlarge` instance provides 16 GiB of memory per CPU core (384 GiB / 24 CPU), satisfying the optimization goal. A `nodeSelector` has been added to ensure the job runs on this specific instance type.

```yaml
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 4
```

result.item:
Hello! As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the provided code and error logs. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the failure is a missing shared library at runtime. The key error message from the logs is:

```
amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This error, combined with the exit code `127`, indicates that when the `amg` executable was launched, the dynamic linker could not find the required OpenMP library (`libgomp.so.1`).

Although the application container's Dockerfile correctly installs the `libgomp1` package, the environment set up by the Flux framework's launcher container does not correctly point to the library's location.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we must explicitly tell the application where to find its required libraries by setting the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable. The standard location for this library in an Ubuntu 22.04-based container is `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`.

I will add this environment variable to your application container definition within the MiniCluster manifest.

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
    environment:
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:tag-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 4
```

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest reinstates the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable,
# which has been identified as the correct solution for the persistent
# "libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file" error. This ensures the
# dynamic linker can find the required OpenMP libraries at runtime.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg-test-aws
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for a single-node execution.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) to run.
  tasks: 4

  # Keep pods and logs after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Retry the job at most once upon failure.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Pod-specific settings for the MiniCluster.
  pod:
    # Do not restart pods if they fail; let the job controller handle it.
    restartPolicy: Never

  # Flux Operator logging settings.
  logging:
    # Fail on any non-zero exit code.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute the AMG benchmark with the required problem and a small test size.
      command: "amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4"
      # The application container is a worker, not a launcher, per instructions.
      launcher: false
      # Environment variables to fix runtime errors and control threading.
      environment:
        # Constrain OpenMP to a single thread per task to avoid oversubscription.
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        # Explicitly set the library path to resolve the "libgomp.so.1" loading error.
        # This includes paths for both x86_64 and arm64 to support the multi-arch container.
        LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu

result.item:
An analysis of the error log indicates the job failed because the application could not find a required shared library.

### ERROR ANALYSIS

The key error message from the logs is:
`amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`

This, combined with the container's exit code of `127`, points to a missing runtime dependency. The `libgomp.so.1` library is essential for running applications compiled with OpenMP support. The `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` currently set in the manifest does not include the directory where this library is located within the container.

### PROPOSED FIX

To resolve this, I will update the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to include `/usr/lib64`, a standard location for such libraries.

Additionally, to align with the optimization and testing goals you provided, I will make the following changes:
1.  **Select an Optimal Instance:** I have chosen the `r6a.12xlarge` instance, which provides the best memory-per-core ratio (16 GiB/core) and a high core count (24), satisfying the optimization goal. A `nodeSelector` will be added to target this instance.
2.  **Update Tasks and Command:** The number of tasks will be set to 24 to match the vCPU count of the selected instance, preventing oversubscription. The command is updated to a larger problem size as instructed for optimization.
3.  **Add Optimization Environment Variable:** The `OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism` variable will be added as suggested.
4.  **Enable Quiet Logging:** Logging will be set to quiet to reduce noise.

Here is the corrected Job manifest:

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-aws
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The backoffLimit is set to 1 as requested
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 128 128 128 -P 4 3 2
    environment:
      # Fix: Added /usr/lib64 to the library path to find libgomp.so.1
      LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu:/usr/lib64
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
      # Added suggested optimization variable
      OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  logging:
    # Enabled quiet logging as requested
    quiet: true
  pod:
    restartPolicy: Never
    spec:
      # Added nodeSelector to target the optimal instance
      nodeSelector:
        node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
  # Set size to 1 node as required
  size: 1
  # Increased tasks to match the vCPU count of the selected node
  tasks: 24
```

**Analysis of the Error:**

The job failed with an exit code of 127. The logs show the specific reason for this failure:

```
amg: error while loading shared libraries: libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This indicates that the `amg` application, which is compiled with OpenMP for threading, cannot find its required OpenMP runtime library (`libgomp.so.1`) in the container's environment. The existing `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` does not include the directory where this library is located.

Additionally, the job manifest is missing a `nodeSelector` to target a specific instance type, which is a requirement for the optimization task.

**Recommended Solution:**

To resolve the library issue, we must update the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variable to include the path where system software libraries are stored in this container. Based on the file paths visible in the logs (e.g., `/opt/software/...`), a likely location for these libraries is `/opt/software/lib64`.

To fulfill the optimization requirements, I have also selected an instance type that maximizes the memory per CPU core. The `r6a.12xlarge` instance provides 16 GiB of memory per CPU core (384 GiB / 24 CPU), satisfying the optimization goal. A `nodeSelector` has been added to ensure the job runs on this specific instance type.

import math
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal
import json

def evaluate_amg_run(
    # Problem size
    problem_size: Any,
    total_ranks: int,
    nodes_used: int,
    # Hardware constraints
    cores_per_node: int,
    memory_gb_per_node: int,
    threading_hint: int,
    current_fom: float,
    threshold: float = 0.90,
    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 4.5e8,
    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 1.0e6,
    dofs_per_gb: float = 1.2e7,
    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.95
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Args:
        problem_size (tuple): The 3D problem grid dimensions (e.g., Px, Py, Pz).
        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.
        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.
        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.
        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.
        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).
        current_fom (float): The measured Figure of Merit (FOM) from the completed run.
        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum FOM (default 0.90).
        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 4.5e8).
        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant modeling communication overhead (default 1.0e6).
        dofs_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (DOFs per GB of RAM, default 1.2e7).
        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.95).

    Returns:
        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.
    """   
    total_dofs = problem_size[0] * problem_size[1] * problem_size[2]
    if total_ranks == 0:
        return {"decision": "RETRY", "reason": "The number of tasks cannot be zero. Suggest using at least one task."}

    # --- 2. Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---
    dofs_per_rank = total_dofs / total_ranks
    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint
    cpu_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node

    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(dofs_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)
    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency
    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_ranks * cpu_per_rank

    performance_ratio = 0.0
    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:
        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom

    estimated_memory_gb = total_dofs / dofs_per_gb
    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used)

    metrics = {
        "performance_ratio": round(performance_ratio, 3),
        "scaling_efficiency": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),
        "memory_utilization": round(memory_utilization, 3),
        "dofs_per_rank": int(dofs_per_rank),
        "theoretical_max_fom": f"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}"
    }
    # --- 3. Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---        
    # Primary STOP condition: Performance is good enough.
    if performance_ratio >= threshold:
        return {
            "decision": "STOP",
            "reason": f"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Primary RETRY condition: Memory is the bottleneck.
    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The problem size is too large for the allocated memory. Suggest significantly reducing the problem size.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Secondary RETRY condition: Scaling is the bottleneck.
    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for "low" efficiency
         return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the problem size per rank is too small. Suggest significantly increasing the problem size to provide more work per rank.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Tertiary RETRY condition: Cores are underutilized on a single node.
    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Suggest increasing the number of tasks to better utilize the hardware.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Default RETRY condition: Performance is simply not good enough yet.
    return {
        "decision": "RETRY",
        "reason": f"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Suggest moderately increasing the problem size to improve the work-per-rank and move closer to the optimal FOM.",
        "metrics": metrics
    }
